text: drygate gates on duplication with jscpd rather than a detector of its own
author: claude-code
rationale: No existing plugin blocks a turn on new duplication; jscpd already has baselines, isNew in its JSON report and an MCP server
revisit: jscpd stops being maintained, or another plugin ships a working duplication gate
choice: Wrap jscpd 5.4.x (MIT, Rust binary, token clone detection with renamed and baseline support)
alternatives: PMD CPD: Java, about 36 s on 547 files in jscpd's own benchmark against 84 ms
Adopt DRYwall: on-demand refactor plugin with no gate

text: The baseline is a snapshot of the working tree taken at SessionStart, not a git ref
author: claude-code
cost_if_wrong: Clones the agent commits before the gate runs slip through, or the user's WIP blocks the agent
choice: SessionStart runs jscpd --update-baseline into a per-session file; Stop compares the tree against it
alternatives: jscpd --changed: rebuilds its baseline when HEAD moves, so a clone the agent commits mid-session is never reported (seen in a probe)
--baseline-from-ref with HEAD at session start: reports the user's own uncommitted clones as new

text: A clone blocks only when its file pair has more clones than at session start
author: claude-code
cost_if_wrong: An agent that edits one copy of old duplication and adds a new copy between the same two files is not blocked
choice: Count clones per file pair in the baseline report and in the Stop report; block the new clones of any pair whose count grew
alternatives: Block every isNew clone: editing one literal inside an existing clone changes its fingerprint and blocks (seen in a probe), so old debt blocks unrelated work

text: SessionStart snapshots in a detached process, and Stop skips the scan when nothing changed since the last pass
author: claude-code
rationale: Measured on w-combinator: SessionStart 5.6 s synchronous vs 0.1 s detached; repeat Stop 2.4 s vs 0.15 s
revisit: Headless runs (flocc) report false blocks from the snapshot race
cost_if_wrong: A clone that existed before, in a file the agent edits before the snapshot finishes, counts as added and blocks once
choice: SessionStart spawns the snapshot and returns; Stop waits up to 90 s for it; files modified after SessionStart are left out of the snapshot; Stop compares a HEAD + git status + mtime fingerprint against the last passing check
alternatives: Synchronous snapshot: 3 to 6 s before the first prompt on a 193k-line Unity repo, plus the one-time npm install

text: Worktrees, submodules and nested clones inside the repo are always left out of the scan
author: claude-code
rationale: kairos: .claude/worktrees produced 16,841 of the clone sides and 3 s per Stop; a worktree created mid-session blocked the turn
choice: Read git worktree list, gitlinks and untracked dirs holding .git, and add them to the one --ignore flag along with the repo's own .jscpd.json ignore list

text: The stdlib and empty-wrapper check is an on-demand sweep, not part of the stop gate
author: claude-code
rationale: The user asked for a sweep review with haiku plus sonnet; a haiku-only pass names APIs that do not exist

evidence.ref: live run on a planted fixture: 3 confirmed, 2 traps rejected, 0.33 USD

cost_if_wrong: Duplication of stdlib behavior added between sweeps reaches main unchecked
choice: /drygate:sweep: haiku scout agents read batches of ~2,000 lines and list candidates; sonnet verifier agents confirm each against the code, its call sites and the real API; only CONFIRMED findings are reported
alternatives: Per-turn self-review of new functions: the model reviews its own code
Independent agent hook on every code-changing stop: a paid model call per turn per teammate, Claude Code only

text: A clone blocks only when both its file pair and its code are more common than in the snapshot, and the snapshot moves forward after each pass
author: claude-code
rationale: Review reproduced rename false blocks, accepted duplicates re-blocking every turn, and pulled commits blocking a resumed session
cost_if_wrong: Removing one clone and adding a different one between the same two files in one turn is not caught
choice: Tally clones per file pair and per hash of the whitespace-normalised fragment; block a clone when both counts grew; save the current tally after a passing stop and after a second stop lets duplicates through; take a new snapshot on resume, leaving out uncommitted files changed since the last check
alternatives: Pair count only (d3): renaming a file with an old clone forms a new pair and blocked
jscpd isNew only: editing inside an old clone changes its fingerprint and blocked
